w:r.w:t: This document provides complete instructions for building and deploying the AralMate MVP as a secure, production-ready responsive web application. It is intended for the dev team to review, comment on, and implement.
The MVP is a single-file responsive web app (HTML/CSS/JS).
It uses Kimi K2.5 vision API to analyze photos of school materials.
Alon generates a lesson explanation, a 5-question quiz, and 8 flashcards.
No chat, no voice input. Photo in → AI output out.
aralmate.html — The front-end app, hosted on Vercel
worker.js — The Cloudflare Worker proxy (holds the Kimi API key securely)
This document — Build and deployment guide for the dev team

The core problem: any API key placed inside a browser HTML file is fully visible to anyone who opens DevTools. This is a real security risk — the key could be stolen and used to run up charges on the Kimi account.
The solution is a two-layer deployment:
What the user sees and interacts with
Holds the Kimi key, forwards requests

The user's browser (Chrome on Android) never communicates directly with Kimi. Every request goes through the Worker. The Kimi API key is stored as an encrypted environment variable on Cloudflare — it is never in the HTML file and never visible in the browser.
User's phone — Alon displays the result
The X-AralMate-Secret is a shared secret between the Worker and the HTML app.
It is NOT the Kimi API key. It is a simple passphrase you choose (e.g. "aralmate-2026").
Its purpose: prevent random people who find the Worker URL from using it.
The Kimi API key itself is stored only in Cloudflare — never in the HTML file.

The Worker is a small piece of server-side JavaScript that runs on Cloudflare's global network. It does exactly three things: validates the secret header, attaches the Kimi API key, and proxies the request.
Create a new file called worker.js with the following content:
// AralMate Cloudflare Worker — Kimi API Proxy
// Set KIMI_API_KEY and ARALMATE_SECRET as encrypted env variables.
The Worker needs two encrypted environment variables. These are set in the Cloudflare dashboard — never in the code.
Your Kimi API key from Moonshot AI dashboard
The actual Kimi API key — stored encrypted on Cloudflare
Shared secret between Worker and HTML app — prevents unauthorized access
3.3 Cloudflare setup steps (UI only — no terminal)
Follow these steps exactly in order:
Go to cloudflare.com and create a free account.
From the dashboard, click "Workers & Pages" in the left sidebar.
Click "Create" → "Create Worker". Give it the name: aralmate-proxy.
Replace all the default code in the editor with the worker.js code above.
You will see a Worker URL like: https://aralmate-proxy.YOUR-SUBDOMAIN.workers.dev — copy this URL.
Go to your Worker → "Settings" → "Variables and Secrets".
Click "Add" → Type → choose "Secret". Name: KIMI_API_KEY. Value: your Kimi API key. Click Save.
Repeat: Add another Secret. Name: ARALMATE_SECRET. Value: your chosen passphrase. Click Save.
Redeploy the Worker by going back to the Editor tab and clicking "Save and Deploy" again.
After Step 10, your Worker is live. You can test it by sending a POST request from Postman or curl.
The Worker URL will look like: https://aralmate-proxy.yourname.workers.dev
This is the URL you will paste into the HTML app in Section 5.
The front-end is a single HTML file. It uses plain HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript — no framework, no build step. This keeps it simple, fast, and easy to update.
Alon greeting, two buttons: Take Photo + Choose from Gallery
Alon animation with wave bars, status message while Kimi processes
Alon explains the topic. Text with vocabulary highlights. Simplify toggle.
5 multiple-choice questions. One at a time. Score shown at end.
8 flip cards. Tap to flip between term and definition.
The app makes a single POST request per photo. This call goes to the Cloudflare Worker URL, not directly to Kimi.
The prompt instructs Kimi to return structured JSON. The app parses this JSON and renders the lesson, quiz, and flashcards.
You are Alon, a friendly Filipino elementary school tutor.
A Grade 4 student named Miguel has shown you a photo of their school material.
Analyze the image and respond ONLY with valid JSON in this exact structure.
No preamble, no markdown, no explanation outside the JSON.
"alon_intro": "1-2 warm sentences from Alon introducing the topic (bilingual OK)",
"simplified": "Simpler version using shorter sentences, for struggling readers"
These values must be set at the top of the HTML file before deployment:
const APP_SECRET = "aralmate-2026"; // must match ARALMATE_SECRET in Cloudflare
const TALA_COUNT = 145; // starting Tala balance (can be 0)
The app must use the established AralMate design tokens. No deviations.
Primary interactive color, links, active states
Fonts: Nunito (body, weights 400/600/700/800) + Baloo 2 (headings/display, weights 600/700/800). Both loaded from Google Fonts.

The Alon Sarimanok SVG is defined in the existing aralmate_tutor_screen.html mockup file. Dev team must copy the <svg> element from that file — do not redesign or replace it. The bobbing animation (translateY 0 → -10px, 3s ease-in-out infinite) must be preserved.
Vercel hosts the HTML file and provides a public URL your son can access from his Android phone. No server management, no configuration files needed for a single HTML file.
5.1 Vercel setup steps (UI only — no terminal)
Go to vercel.com and create a free account (sign up with email or GitHub).
From the Vercel dashboard, click "Add New" → "Project".
Choose "Browse" or drag and drop the aralmate.html file directly.
Vercel will auto-detect it as a static file. Click "Deploy".
After 30 seconds, Vercel gives you a URL like: https://aralmate.vercel.app
Open that URL on your son's Android phone in Chrome.
Chrome will show "Add to Home Screen" prompt. Tap it. App icon appears on home screen.
When you update the HTML file, go back to Vercel → Deployments → re-upload the new file.
The URL stays the same — your son does not need to update anything on his phone.
Vercel free tier supports unlimited deployments and bandwidth for small apps like this.

The default Vercel URL (aralmate-abc123.vercel.app) is functional but not memorable. If you want a cleaner URL like aralmate.app, you can connect a custom domain in Vercel settings. This is optional for the MVP — not required.

ACTION REQUIRED before going live: Set a monthly spending cap on the Kimi/Moonshot AI account.
Log in to platform.moonshot.cn → Billing → Spending Limit.
Recommended cap for personal/family use: $5-10 USD per month.
This prevents any unexpected charges if the app is used heavily or the Worker URL leaks.
